newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Leftists urge global campaign against APEC.
newsitem.headline: Leftists urge global campaign against APEC.

text.p: Leftists from 24 countries on Saturday appealed for a world campaign to stop an APEC free trade bloc, saying it would tighten a U.S. grip on the Asia-Pacific region.

Delegates to the People's Conference against Imperialist Globalisation issued the call on the eve of a protest motorcade to the APEC summit site at Subic Bay, the former giant U.S. Navy base northwest of Manila.
Organisers said they expected 20,000 people to take part, and said transport strikes and other demonstrations would follow in major cities on the day of the summit itself on Monday.
U.S. President Bill Clinton and China's Jiang Zemin are among heads of government attending the summit of the 18-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.

"We... hereby collectively resolve to oppose globalisation in every way and by every means possible in our respective countries and worldwide," pledged the meeting, attended by more than 200 academics, union leaders and social activists.

"With NAFTA (North America Free Trade Area) in its tight grip, the U.S. has seized the initiative in APEC to regain pre-eminence over Japan in the Pacific, check China's growing influence and consolidate U.S. geopolitical hegemony in the region," it said.

Conference chairman and Filipino leftist leader Satur Ocampo said police had offered to provide security to the leftists' planned motorcade and march to Subic Bay in an apparent bid to head off possible violence.
Police have expressed fears of terrorist violence, including bombings and assassinations, aimed at disrupting the summit.
The United States on Friday warned Americans they might be targetted and to take security precautions.
